title: PROBE: Dense Process Rewards with Observation Evidence for Tool-Augmented Visual Reasoning

problem.claim: Tool-augmented reasoning aims to improve multimodal large language models by offloading perception to external tools.

gap.claim: Existing methods leave incomplete process supervision, tool hallucination, and observation hallucination unsupervised at the trajectory level.

contributions.claim: PROBE uses atomic visual rubrics to drive rubric-guided cold-start trajectory selection, rubric-conditioned per-step tool rewards, and a trajectory-level Visual Rubric Reward.

PROBE-GRPO adds graph-based tool-output utilisation rewards, entailment-based observation-faithfulness rewards, and adaptive learning for unseen tools through identifier obfuscation and description diversification.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that PROBE-7B surpasses proprietary models on multiple structured-reasoning benchmarks.
The authors report that PROBE-7B exhibits self-adaptive tool-use behaviours under novel tool definitions.

narrative_sequence.summary: Tool augmentation is positioned as a way to improve multimodal reasoning by delegating perception to external tools.
Prior methods are described as failing to supervise skipped sub-goals, unused cited tools, and misquoted tool outputs.
PROBE centers trajectory selection and reward design on atomic visual rubrics.
PROBE-GRPO adds tool-output utilisation, observation-fidelity, and unseen-tool adaptation mechanisms.
PROBE-7B is reported to outperform proprietary models on structured-reasoning benchmarks and adapt to novel tool definitions.

source_observation.claim: Trajectory-level failures include skipped sub-goals, unused cited tools, and misquoted tool outputs.

interpretation.claim: Process supervision may need to evaluate both whether tools are used and whether their outputs are faithfully incorporated.

application.claim: Tool-augmented reasoning systems can incorporate step-level tool-use rewards and observation-fidelity checks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these reward mechanisms generalize beyond the reported benchmarks and tool settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, baseline configurations, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the training data, model-training procedure, or implementation details.
The abstract does not report failure cases, ablations, or tool-definition coverage.
